value.title: Reshape and s04 follow-ups: retire, merge, lineage import, batch assign, fixes
value.summary: Delivers req-28 (C26, PEC: communities are reshaped as the work changes) with `pij directory retire` and `merge`, as new roadmap step s15; plus s04 follow-ups from review and the dogfood: closed-seat lineage, batch assign, the latent same-second test, zoned dates.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: From #122's review (F003) and the dogfood (F13, F15, F16). F14 (ddocs renders <did> in code spans as an entity) is a ddocs issue, out of scope.

sections.name: goals
value: Follow-ups from s04's review and the wave B dogfood: record closed seats in lineage, assign many holders in one commit, fix the latent same-second test, and stamp changelog dates with a zone.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: F15, lineage import. `pij directory lineage add <role>[/<instance>] <seat> --from <time> --to <time> --why <text>` lets the prime record a closed seat's past holding (no live seat needed), validated against overlaps; refused for anyone but the prime.
F16, batch assign. `pij directory assign --batch <file>` (role, instance, seat lines) records many holders in one writer commit, all or nothing.

F003, the latent flake. The same-second HTTP test from #122 stops assuming a wall-clock second (inject the clock or drop the precondition) and keeps proving that rapid assign, release and reassign never collide.
F13, zones. Changelog and holder dates written by the writer carry an explicit zone (RFC 3339 with offset or Z), and the view prints the local time with its zone.

Retire (req-28). `pij directory retire <role> --why <text>` marks a role retired by a writer commit with a changelog row; it refuses while the role has a live holder (release first) or queued requests (s05), naming them. Its memory, outputs and lineage stay readable, and `pij directory` lists it as retired, not missing; `--json` carries the state. Sends to a retired role refuse by name.

Merge (req-28). `pij directory merge <from> --into <to> --why <text>` retires <from> pointing at <to> in one writer commit (both roles' changelogs get a row; <from>'s memory and outputs stay where they are and are listed under <to> as merged-from). Both roles' memory, outputs and lineage are preserved and stay readable afterwards (none moved or rewritten). A send to <from> afterwards refuses and names <to>.

Roadmap step s15 (pm-001's decision, reported to the prime). In this PR, roadmap 001 gains step s15 'Reshape: retire and merge roles', delivering req-28, depending on s04, with its plan cell set to docs/plans/206-directory-followups, state complete; req-28 goes to shipped. PR #125 (which adds req-28) must merge first.

F18 (low, from the prime): a hand commit in the standing governance worktree can fail on index.lock while the daemon's writer is committing there (seen 06 Nov: the prime's commit raced the close writer's 655c0b6). While it holds the index, the writer leaves a short-lived marker naming itself (for example .git/pij-writer.owner with seat, pid and time, removed on exit); the community README tells humans to retry after a moment when they see it; and the writer's own commits retry briefly on a foreign index.lock (bounded), then refuse by name.

F17 (low): a seat holding two roles gets the last assign's window name. The window is named for the seat's primary holding (the earliest open one), or `<project>:<role1>+<role2>`; pick one, and say so in the docs.

F19 (medium, s03 dogfood): `pij directory template-diff <id>` on a role with a `template` but no `template_version` refuses with a misleading E-RS-ARG ('template_version "" is not a version number', next null; directory.rs:251 unwrap_or_default). It should say the role records no template version, and name the fix (record one with the edit verb from F20).

F20 (medium, s03 dogfood; needed for reshape, req-28): `pij directory edit <id> --why <text> (--set <field>=<value>... | --file <json>)` changes an existing role through the writer (validate, build, commit, changelog row). Today add refuses an existing role, so imported roles can't be corrected without hand edits.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Batch assign is one writer commit for many holders (cheaper than one each); lineage add is one commit. Retire and merge are one writer commit each. No timer or poll.

Docs and states. Docs: docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents retire and merge; difficulties.md rows F13, F15, F16 and #122 F003 marked resolved. No roadmap state changes (follow-up work). docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.value: Code to read first: crates/daemon/src/community/ (holders, directory), crates/daemon/tests/pr122_review/, the dogfood report (governance roles/docs-system/outputs/2026-11/wave-b-dogfood.md). No migration expected.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
